title: Birbal's Wisdom vs Tansen's Music
summary: Akbar asks whether Tansen's heavenly music or Birbal's sharp wit is more essential to the empire. Birbal orchestrates a gentle demonstration.
full_text:
One tranquil evening in the courtyard of Fatehpur Sikri, the legendary musician Mian Tansen sang Raga Deepak. His voice was so sublime, so rich with spiritual resonance, that oil lamps throughout the pavilion flickered and blossomed into flame, and wild deer from the forest gathered near the stone arches, transfixed by the divine melody.

Emperor Akbar sat in rapturous bliss. When the final note faded into the scented night breeze, Akbar exclaimed: 'Mian Tansen, your music is the supreme glory of Hindustan! Surely, music is the highest gift bestowed upon mankind. What say you, Birbal? Can mere wit and statecraft compare to the celestial magic of Tansen's art?'

Birbal bowed respectfully to both the Emperor and the great musician: 'Sire, Mian Tansen's music is indeed a bridge between earth and heaven. Yet art can flourish only where wisdom and security protect life.'

Akbar smiled skeptically: 'Are you claiming that your riddles and court counsel are more vital than divine melody?'

'Let us test the truth tomorrow, Your Majesty,' Birbal suggested.

The next afternoon, Akbar, Birbal, and Tansen went hunting in the wilderness. Birbal arranged for the royal party to become separated from the main escort. Suddenly, from the dense bamboo thicket, an enraged wild elephant with flared ears and raised tusks charged directly at the three men!

Akbar drew his sword, but an elephant cannot be stopped by a blade. 'Tansen!' Akbar shouted in panic. 'Sing Raga Megh Malhar! Soothe this beast with your celestial music!'

Trembling with mortal terror, Tansen opened his mouth, but only hoarse, quivering squeaks emerged from his parched throat. The charging beast drew closer, shaking the earth!

Birbal acted in a flash. He grabbed a heavy woolen hunting blanket from his saddle, wrapped it around a dry tamarind bough, struck a flint spark to ignite it into a roaring ball of flame, and hurled it directly before the charging beast's feet while banging two bronze hunting horns together with ear-splitting clatter.

Terrified by the sudden explosion of fire and noise, the rogue elephant wheeled around and crashed back into the forest.

Catching his breath, Emperor Akbar leaned against his horse. Birbal smiled gently at the trembling musician and the Emperor:

'Your Majesty, when the mind is at peace, Tansen's music enchants the soul and brings tears of joy. But when the rogue elephant of danger charges, it is presence of mind and practical wisdom that saves our lives so we may live to hear Tansen sing another day!'

Akbar embraced both Tansen and Birbal, declaring that his court was blessed beyond measure to possess both the soul of art and the shield of wisdom.
